requirements.title: Add omni update: 3-way-merge template improvements into adopted workspaces

If make_ai.py itself changes, update automatically re-runs sync in a fresh process so entrypoint/pointer/ignore files regenerate from the new templates. omni doctor gained a matching check warning when .ai/omni-version.json is missing. Also adds `--bootstrap` to `omni update` (records --source's current ref as the starting point without merging anything, for a workspace adopted before update-tracking existed) and a README Quick Start section covering the adopt/doctor/update loop end to end, including the bootstrap path, since a working feature nobody can find or follow doesn't solve the 'clunky to integrate' complaint either.

requirements.title: Add omni graph: a deterministic tree-sitter AST code graph, not a vector index
requirements.description: Adds `omni graph build/trace/show`, a new omni_graph.py module holding a local, deterministic code graph parsed from source with tree-sitter -- no embeddings, no vector store. Every node is a code entity read straight from a syntax tree (module/class/function/method); every edge is tagged EXTRACTED (a fact read directly from a single source site: an import statement, a call site, a base class) or INFERRED (resolved by traversing the graph across files/scopes, or by an optional configured semantic API pass). `omni graph trace <a> <b>` answers 'how are these connected' with an actual shortest path of tagged hops instead of a similarity score; `omni graph show <node>` lists a symbol's direct EXTRACTED/INFERRED edges. Covers Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript in v1. tree-sitter and the per-language grammars are an optional `[graph]` extra so the workspace stays dependency-free by default: `omni graph build` fails with an actionable install message if the extra is missing, while `trace`/`show` only read the JSON `build` wrote and need nothing beyond the standard library. The semantic pass is opt-in via `--semantic` and only calls out to a network API if OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_URL is explicitly configured; its findings are still validated against known graph symbol names before being added as INFERRED edges, so a hallucinated relation can't be written into the graph silently. The CLI surface (subcommand-per-verb, a --json mode on every command) is intentionally 1:1 wrappable by an MCP relay the same way omni_map/omni_doctor/omni_sync already are.
acceptance_criteria: omni graph build parses Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript source with tree-sitter and writes a JSON graph whose edges are each tagged provenance EXTRACTED or INFERRED, with a resolver field distinguishing syntax / graph-traversal / semantic-api.

omni graph build fails with a clear install message (not a traceback) when tree-sitter or a language grammar is missing, verified by running it against the system Python with no [graph] extra installed.

omni graph trace <a> <b> resolves symbol names (preferring real symbols over unresolved external placeholders on a name collision) and prints the shortest path between them as a sequence of tagged hops; ambiguous or missing names are reported, not guessed.
omni graph show <node> lists a symbol's direct outgoing and incoming edges with provenance tags.

Cross-file call/import/inheritance resolution (INFERRED edges) verified against this repository's own make_ai.py plus a scratch TypeScript fixture with a cross-file import, confirming resolved edges are correct and that common built-ins (e.g. print) are excluded from the ambiguous unique-name fallback.
omni graph build/trace/show and the graph JSON never require network access unless --semantic is passed and OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_URL is set.
omni doctor gained a non-blocking check that only validates the graph file's JSON shape when one is present, since building the graph is opt-in.
pyproject.toml exposes tree-sitter + grammars as an optional [graph] extra rather than a hard dependency.
risk_notes: Call/inheritance resolution uses deterministic heuristics (same-module lookup, import-alias resolution, unique-name-in-graph fallback) rather than full type inference; ambiguous or dynamically-dispatched references are correctly left EXTRACTED-only rather than guessed, which is intentional but means some real connections will not surface as INFERRED edges in v1.
Nested function/class definitions declared inside another function's body are attributed to the enclosing function rather than modeled as their own node, to keep v1's traversal bounded.

The semantic pass sends a symbol's name, qualified name, and the full list of known symbol qualified_names to the configured API; it is opt-in (--semantic flag plus an explicitly set OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_URL) so nothing leaves the machine by default.

requirements.title: Fix: adopting or updating omni_graph.py must not be able to break every other command
requirements.description: Found by end-to-end testing REQ-015 against a simulated pre-existing application: (1) ADOPTION_CLI_FILES only listed omni/make_ai.py, so `omni adopt --include-cli` copied a make_ai.py that unconditionally imports omni_graph without ever copying omni_graph.py itself, crashing every single omni command (not just `graph`) in the adopted project with a raw ModuleNotFoundError. (2) Testing the upgrade path (a project adopted before omni_graph.py existed, running `omni update` against a source that now has it) surfaced a deeper, structural gap: `omni update`'s file list (TEMPLATE_MANAGED_FILES) is evaluated by the OLD make_ai.py that is currently running the update, not by the newer --source -- so a target can never discover a brand-new template-managed file on the very first update after it's introduced, no matter what that file list contains by the time of a *later* update. Fixed both: added omni_graph.py to ADOPTION_CLI_FILES (fixes fresh `omni adopt --include-cli` immediately, and fixes `omni update` from the second update onward once a target is running post-fix code), and made make_ai.py's own `import omni_graph` defensive (try/except, falls back to None) with a shared require_omni_graph() guard on every `omni graph ...` subcommand and a doctor warning -- so a target still missing omni_graph.py (the unavoidable one-time gap on that very first update, or any other reason the file might be absent) degrades to 'omni graph is unavailable' instead of taking down doctor/sync/map/every other command.
acceptance_criteria: omni adopt --target <dir> --include-cli copies omni_graph.py alongside make_ai.py, verified against a scratch pre-existing application directory whose own pre-existing files (README, source, .gitignore) are confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged after adoption.

A project simulated as adopted before omni_graph.py existed (sourced from OmniEngineering@523c47b) that runs `omni update` against a current source no longer crashes: omni doctor, omni sync, and every non-graph command work immediately after that update even though omni_graph.py is still absent on that specific first pass, with a clear doctor warning naming the gap and the fix (re-run omni adopt --include-cli or omni update).

The same project's second `omni update` (now running the fixed make_ai.py) reports 'added: omni_graph.py', after which omni graph build/trace/show all work against the adopted project's own source files.

Adopter-owned files (.ai/project-configuration.md, .ai/project-map.md, .ai/requirements/requirements.json, CHANGELOG.md) verified untouched by both update passes in this test, including a deliberately added custom note/entry in each.
omni doctor and omni graph both continue to work correctly in this repo's own working copy (which always has omni_graph.py) after these changes.
risk_notes: The structural update-mechanism gap (a target's own running code decides what files it looks for) is not fully eliminated -- it is closed for every template file added from this point forward (once a target has updated past this fix, it will correctly discover any future new template file on the very next update), but a project that adopted before omni_graph.py existed will still see one warning-but-not-broken update before omni_graph.py actually arrives. A fully general fix would have run_update ask --source's own make_ai.py for its current file manifest via subprocess instead of trusting its own constant; deferred as a larger structural change beyond this fix's scope.

The defensive import is the durable half of this fix: it guarantees a missing omni_graph.py (for this reason or any other -- a bad copy, manual deletion) degrades to one feature being unavailable rather than the whole CLI being unusable, independent of whether the file-list gap above is ever fully closed.

requirements.title: Add omni graph render: a permanent, stdlib-only SVG visualization command
requirements.description: REQ-018's node-link graph was a one-off script requiring networkx+numpy, run by hand and copied into the repo. User ask: this should be a permanent feature of omni itself that updates as the user's project updates, not a one-off artifact. Added `omni graph render` (and the underlying omni_graph.render()/_spring_layout()/_render_svg()/_ego_network() functions): renders .ai/project-graph.json as a force-directed node-link SVG using a small pure-Python Fruchterman-Reingold layout -- no numpy/networkx dependency, so render works with just the standard library exactly like trace/show (only build needs the [graph] extra). Nodes are colored by source language (python/javascript/typescript) and sized by kind (module > class > function/method); edges distinguish calls/imports/inherits (colored, per edge style) from defines (faint, de-emphasized) from related_to (dashed, semantic-pass edges). --max-nodes caps large graphs to the highest-degree nodes to keep the O(n^2) layout fast; --focus/--depth renders just one symbol's neighborhood instead of the whole codebase. design/diagrams/omni-code-graph.svg was regenerated using this actual shipped command (replacing the prior one-off script's output) so the committed diagram is proof the feature works, not just a description of it.
acceptance_criteria: omni graph render writes a well-formed SVG node-link graph from .ai/project-graph.json, verified by parsing the output as XML and rendering it to PNG for visual review.
render works via plain system Python with no tree-sitter or third-party layout library installed, verified by running it without the [graph] extra present.

Layout performance verified empirically: 112 real nodes rendered in ~0.2s, 300 nodes (max-nodes cap, including external references) in ~1.3s against this repo's own graph -- fast enough for normal CLI use.
--focus <symbol> --depth N renders only that symbol's N-hop neighborhood, verified against run_doctor at depth 1 producing a correct, legible ego-network.
--max-nodes correctly truncates to the highest-degree nodes and reports truncated:true, verified by rendering with include_external=True against a cap below the real node count.
The project's own root label in the rendered title resolves to a real folder name instead of a literal '.', verified before and after the fix.
design/diagrams/omni-code-graph.svg in this repo is the literal output of running `omni graph render` against this repo, not a hand-tuned or separately-scripted render.

omni doctor and omni graph build/trace/show continue to pass after these changes; .ai/project-graph.svg (the default output path) is gitignored the same way .ai/project-graph.json is, since it's a heavy, regeneratable, opt-in artifact, not a committed navigation aid.
risk_notes: The layout is O(n^2) per iteration (a deliberate simplicity/dependency tradeoff over numpy-vectorized force-directed algorithms), which is why --max-nodes defaults to 300 and truncates by degree rather than rendering arbitrarily large graphs unbounded.

Dense, highly-connected clusters (e.g. this repo's own doctor-validator cluster) still show some label overlap at default settings -- an inherent characteristic of force-directed layouts at this node density, not something --max-nodes or --focus fully eliminates; --focus on a smaller neighborhood is the escape hatch for a specific area.

requirements.title: Fix mobile app-close/lock session handling: stop the AppState background listener from over-firing
requirements.description: The login screen, biometric unlock, and the sign-out-on-close behavior in mobile/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx were reported as not working properly. Code review (not a device reproduction, since this environment has no simulator/device) found the AppState 'background' listener that locks or fully logs out a signed-in user was reacting to the raw 'background' event with no debounce. Android has no 'inactive' state, so the account screen's own photo-library/camera picker (mobile/app/(app)/account.tsx, via expo-image-picker) and the Google sign-in browser tab (mobile/src/auth/googleSignIn.ts, via expo-web-browser on both iOS and Android) all report as 'background' too, even though the user never left the app. That immediately locked or logged out a signed-in user mid-task on those flows. Added a short grace period (1500ms) that cancels itself if 'active' returns before it fires, so a transient system-UI interruption is absorbed while a genuine app close or screen lock -- which lasts far longer than the window -- still locks/logs out exactly as before. Login, biometric enrollment/unlock, and the cold-start session-resolution logic were also read closely; no other functional defect was found there.
acceptance_criteria: Backgrounding the app for longer than the grace window still locks a biometric-enrolled device or signs out a non-biometric one, unchanged from prior behavior.

Returning to 'active' before the grace window elapses (the shape of a permission dialog, the in-app photo/camera picker, or the Google sign-in browser tab) does not lock or sign out a previously signed-in user.
A hard OS kill during the grace window is still caught on next launch by the existing cold-start session-resolution branch, so no session survives a real close.
mobile typecheck (tsc --noEmit) passes with no new errors.
risk_notes: Verified by static code review and `tsc --noEmit` only -- this environment has no iOS/Android simulator or device, so the actual background/foreground timing (photo picker, camera, Google sign-in browser handoff) still needs a manual pass on a real device or simulator before release.

The 1500ms grace window is a judgment call, not a spec'd value -- long enough to absorb a permission-dialog or picker hand-off, short enough that a real screen-lock or app-switch away still locks/signs out promptly. Worth revisiting if real-device testing shows it too short (a slow Android photo-library launch) or unnecessarily long.

requirements.title: Fix login-screen autofill: password did not follow a tapped email suggestion

A value picked from that suggestion list is therefore just an email address, with no password attached to bring along. register.tsx already paired its equivalent field correctly (textContentType="username" + autoComplete="username"); login.tsx did not match it. Changed login's email field to autoComplete="username" and added importantForAutofill="yes" to both the email and password fields (the explicit Android autofill opt-in some providers key off of). Widened the shared TextField component's prop passthrough (mobile/src/components/ui.tsx) to allow importantForAutofill, which it did not previously forward.

TextField's prop type accepts importantForAutofill without a TypeScript error.

requirements.title: Persist a plain native login across a full app close
requirements.description: The cold-start effect in AuthContext.tsx only attempted to resume a session via refresh() on web. requirements.title: Stop eas update from shipping the dev-machine LAN API URL
requirements.description: The REQ-029/030 OTA update published to the preview channel on 2026-09-18 was exported with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL still resolved from mobile/.env.local (http://10.0.0.85:3000, the dev machine LAN address used for local expo start testing) instead of the production backend baked into the real preview/production native builds via eas.json. @expo/env loads .env.local unconditionally ahead of any NODE_ENV-specific file, and eas update runs its export locally using whatever is in the shell/dotenv at the time -- it does not read eas.json build profiles' env blocks the way eas build does. Every network call in that update (password login, the Google sign-in code-for-token exchange against our own backend, anything server-backed) would have silently failed for any device off that LAN. Republished immediately with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL explicitly set on the command line to override it.

Publishing an update this way is documented so it is not repeated from memory alone.
risk_notes: No code changed -- this is a publishing-process fix, not an app-code fix. The underlying eas.json / .env.local layout is unchanged, so the same mistake is possible again on any future eas update run from this machine unless EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL is set explicitly each time.

Not verified against the actual installed app on a physical device in this environment; the fix is confirmed at the export/bundle level (matching manifest permalink query and a local re-export using the same working directory and .env.local), not by a live device check.

requirements.title: Stop a plain logout from disabling biometric unlock
requirements.description: mobile/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx's logout() called clearBiometricEnrollment() unconditionally, the same full device-enrollment wipe used by logoutAll() (sign out of every session) and useFallbackSignIn() (explicit "use password instead"). That meant a user who turned biometric unlock on, then just logged out normally, found it silently switched back off the next time they signed in -- a device setting resetting itself without the user ever touching it. logout() no longer calls clearBiometricEnrollment(); it only clears the current session (in-memory tokens, plain refresh-token key, revokes the token server-side). logoutAll() and useFallbackSignIn() are unchanged, since both are an explicit choice to drop this device's local shortcut, and unlockWithBiometric() still clears the enrollment if the stored token turns out to be missing or invalid.
acceptance_criteria: Enabling biometric unlock in Settings, then using the regular "Log out" action, leaves biometric unlock enabled the next time the app is opened.
logoutAll() and "use password instead" from the lock screen still fully drop this device's biometric enrollment, same as before.
risk_notes: Not verified on a physical device in this environment -- confirmed by reading the logout/logoutAll/useFallbackSignIn code paths and mobile tsc --noEmit, not a live before/after toggle check.

requirements.title: Make omni map idempotent so the workspace-freshness CI check can pass
requirements.description: The CI job that regenerates .ai/project-map.md and fails the build on any diff (added to catch real drift, see REQ-001-era history) could never actually pass: run_map() in make_ai.py stamped a fresh wall-clock "Generated at" line and rewrote the file unconditionally on every invocation, so a fresh CI run's regenerated file always differed from the committed one by at least that timestamp, even with zero structural changes. This was masked while the file also had genuine content drift (fixed in a prior commit today), then surfaced again immediately -- re-running `omni map` right after committing a fully up-to-date map still showed a diff. run_map() now compares the freshly rendered content against the existing file with the "Generated at" line normalized out first, and only rewrites (bumping the timestamp) when something else actually changed; otherwise it reports Unchanged and leaves the file alone, matching the write-if-changed pattern run_sync() already uses elsewhere in this file.
acceptance_criteria: Running `python3 omni map` twice in a row with no repository changes between the two runs reports "Unchanged" both times and does not modify .ai/project-map.md.
Running `python3 omni map` after a real structural change (a file added or removed under a tracked path) still reports "Updated" and regenerates the file with a fresh timestamp.
risk_notes: This was the actual reason CI kept failing on master even after the prior commit's real content fix -- the timestamp alone guaranteed a diff on every run. No other omni-generated file (handled by run_sync's write_generated_file) had this problem, since that path already normalizes to write-if-changed.

requirements.title: Fix the workspace map so a clean CI checkout actually agrees with what is committed
requirements.description: The omni-workspace CI job kept failing even after REQ-033 made map generation itself idempotent, because two other parts of the generated .ai/project-map.md were environment-dependent rather than a property of the repository: the "Root" line read the literal name of whatever folder the tool happened to run from ("prep-lms" on this machine, "Ascendra" on a GitHub Actions checkout), and the directory walk only ever read the repo-root .gitignore by hand, missing patterns declared in backend/.gitignore and mobile/.gitignore (build/typecheck leftovers like a stale tsconfig.tsbuildinfo or an exported web bundle sitting in backend/public/ on a developer machine that a clean CI checkout never has). Root now comes from the git remote instead of the checkout folder name, and the ignore check asks git itself (git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard) which correctly resolves every nested .gitignore instead of re-parsing just the top-level file.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone of the repository (no local build artifacts, no leftover node_modules/tsbuildinfo output) regenerates .ai/project-map.md identical to what is committed, regardless of the folder name it was cloned into.
git diff --exit-code against the paths the CI workspace-freshness check watches is clean after running omni sync and omni map from a clean checkout.
risk_notes: Verified by cloning the repository to a scratch directory with a different name, pointing its origin remote at the real GitHub URL, and running the exact three commands the CI job runs -- not verified inside an actual GitHub Actions runner.

requirements.title: Stop OTA updates from being offered to native builds they are not actually compatible with
requirements.description: mobile/app.json pinned runtimeVersion to policy "appVersion", so EAS decided whether an OTA update was safe for an installed build purely by the version string ("2.0.0"), which never changed across the 2026-09-18 Expo SDK 51 -> SDK 57 upgrade even though that upgrade changed real native code (React Native itself and other native modules). Any OTA update published after that upgrade would have been offered as compatible to a device still running an SDK-51 native build, where a JS bundle expecting SDK-57 native APIs could crash or misbehave. Confirmed via Run this command inside a project directory. that no update has ever been published to the production channel (the live Play Store build, still SDK 51, was not exposed to this), but the preview channel did receive an update on this policy (REQ-032, group bb44bbd4) before the fix. Switched to policy "fingerprint", which derives compatibility from the actual native project contents so a change like this is caught automatically instead of depending on someone remembering to bump a version number.
acceptance_criteria: mobile/app.json runtimeVersion policy is "fingerprint".
npx expo-doctor and npx eas-cli fingerprint:generate both succeed against the current project.
A new native build is produced before any further OTA update is published, so devices are running a build whose fingerprint matches what future updates will target.
risk_notes: Devices already running the old appVersion-policy preview build will not resolve updates published under the new fingerprint-policy runtime until they install a new native build -- this is expected and matches how the old policy would eventually have needed a new build too, just without automatic protection against a mismatched one in between.

requirements.title: Stop a plain logout revoking the token biometric unlock needs
requirements.description: REQ-032 kept biometric enrolment alive across a plain logout but left no usable credential behind it. With biometrics on the refresh token lives only in the OS-gated store; logout still sent that same live token to /api/auth/logout which revoked it. The next unlock replayed a revoked token at /api/auth/refresh; the backend's rotation guard reads a replay as theft and revokes that token family. A bare catch turned the resulting 401 into silence, so the user saw an unlock that simply did nothing. This exact fix was first written under the REQ-036 id on 2026-09-19 on a short-lived branch (commit 6869276) that was never merged into master -- rediscovered and re-applied here after Nick reported the symptom directly (logging out from the sidebar broke biometric sign-in on the next attempt). Skip the revoke while biometric unlock is enrolled and handle the 401 instead of swallowing it.

logoutAll still revokes server-side, and still clears the biometric enrolment before it does.

requirements.title: Make lesson generation faster and stop regenerate returning near-identical material
requirements.description: Nick reported test/lesson generation and regeneration felt slow especially on network and that regenerating a lesson did not produce different material. requirements.title: Prefetch the next objective's lesson content in the background
requirements.description: Approved follow-up to REQ-062. requirements.title: Weighted cross-format mastery, blueprint readiness, coach guardrails
requirements.description: Owner request 2026-11-07: depth is weighted accuracy across every type of assessment. MODEL (migration 031, mastery_detail; mastery_from_attempts keeps its signature): evidence for (learner, objective) = every graded lesson answer on it (another attempt kind only when its attempt names an assessment_types row) plus every graded PBQ (kind pbq) on its unit (PBQ only adds to objectives with direct answers). Each answer has credit = verdict credit (correct 1, partial 0.5, incorrect 0) x assist credit (none 1, hint 0.5, reveal 0.25, repeat 0.25, retry 0). Assists are read from history as in 029, not only from attempts.assisted: Solo multiple choice and a lesson_hint_reveals row at or before the answer are a hint, an earlier answer to the same stage and question is a repeat; assist_reason 'retry' (revise after feedback, migration 034) also has weight 0, so it is left out of accuracy, is never format evidence and is not counted for Needs review and weight = cognitive weight of its type (guided_step 0.5, multiple_choice 0.75, free_response 1.0, pbq 1.5, explain_back 1.25, scenario 1.5) x unit_scope_factor 0.5 for a unit PBQ x spacing_factor 1.5 if 24h+ after the previous answer on the objective x review_retest_factor 1.2 if the objective/scenario was missed on an earlier day x 0.5^(age days / 60). Weighted accuracy = sum(w*c)/sum(w); readiness score = sum(w*c)/max(sum(w), 2.0). Levels: Needs review (latest direct answer incorrect, 2+ direct answers, accuracy < 0.5); Transfer-ready (accuracy >= 0.75, unassisted correct application-level answers in 2+ format families, first and last 24h+ apart, one of them direct); Independent (accuracy >= 0.60 and one unassisted correct direct free response); Guided (any credit); Introduced. requirements.description: Nick 2026-11-09: release backups are kept 30 days and then dropped automatically within 7 days after.
